mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 3.0%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profits, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate and increases in payroll employment signal a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by high GDP growth and low unemployment), rising housing starts signal sustained consumer demand that supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises in a late-cycle expansion, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in residential investment (RSAFS) indicates strong household demand for housing, which correlates with higher consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS rises, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5%, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate and declines in industrial production signal a monetary tightening coupled with economic slowdown, which reduces corporate profits and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a supply-constrained regime (defined by declining industrial production), a drop in manufacturing output signals reduced capacity utilization and potential inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO declines in a supply-constrained regime, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.
